title: How long until it’s guessed?
instruction: An attacker has stolen a database of passwords and tries 10 billion passwords a second: first well-known passwords, then words and their variations, and finally every combination. Estimate how long the password lasts.
debrief: The attacker first tries well-known passwords, words and their variations. What lasts is a long password: a sentence of unexpected words, or a long random password from a password manager. A different one for every account, plus two-factor authentication.

items.why: One of the most common passwords in the world. It is on the list the attacker tries first.
A popular game and a year. The attacker tries words with numbers at the end among the very first.
A word with a capital letter, a year and an exclamation mark at the end. These are exactly the variations the attacker tries right after plain words.
One word with the usual substitutions. It falls in under a minute.
There are about 6 quadrillion combinations. At 10 billion a second the attacker gets through them in about a week. Length helps more than special characters.

items.q: giraffe eats dumplings on the Moon
items.why: A long sentence of unexpected words. Trying every combination would take about a million years.

items.q: 16 random characters from a password manager
items.why: Twice the length gives so many combinations that it would take far longer than the universe has existed.
